body.target_estimand: \(\tau_{\omega}(P)=\sum_{k=(g,t)\in\mathcal K}\omega_k E_Q[Y_t(g,1)-Y_t(\infty,1)\mid G=g,S=1]\) for any \(Q\in\mathcal M\) inducing \(P\)
body.estimand_functional: \(\tau_{\omega}(P)=\omega'\theta(P)=E_P[\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}\omega_kR_{k,c_0(k),P}(O)]\).  The terminal clean-comparison equalities imply that this also equals \(E_P[b(X)'R_P(O)]\) for every integrable loading satisfying \(A'b(X)=\omega\), both in the localized observed model and in its global OVS subclass.  The published-class efficiency bound is determined separately by projection onto \(\mathcal T_{P,\mathrm{OVS}}\); the localized and aggregate projections are comparison frontiers, not alternative definitions of the causal estimand.

sampling_model.design: Observational staggered adoption in a balanced fixed-\(T\) panel under the global OVS DDD-CPT condition: for every finite treated cohort \(g\), every post period \(u\ge g\), and every period-admissible comparison cohort \(c>u\), the covariate-conditional untreated eligibility gaps agree.
sampling_model.units: \((O_i)_{i=1}^n\) are independent and identically distributed panel units.
sampling_model.treatment: Enabling is absorbing through cohort \(G\), and effective treatment requires \(S=1\).
sampling_model.overlap: Every cohort--eligibility cell in the retained OVS support has conditional probability at least \(\varepsilon\); this includes cells used only by period-admissible normal rows and not by a terminal pairwise score.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: For proved attainment, \(X\) has fixed finite support with masses bounded below.  Fixed-fold training-cell averages estimate all OVS-retained propensities and one-step regressions, the augmented signals \(S_e^{\mathrm{OVS}}=g_e^{\mathrm{OVS}}+Z_e^{\mathrm{OVS}}\), and \(K_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X)\) and \(r_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X)\).  Eigenvalues are thresholded with \(\tau_n=n^{-a}\), \(0<a<1/4\).  In the same fixed-support regime, the comparator gap is evaluated as a finite-dimensional function of cell probabilities, first moments, and second cross-moments, with the same deterministic rank threshold applied to every Moore--Penrose and KKT system.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 4.1 establishes identification, Theorem 4.2 establishes asymptotic normality, and Remark 4.6 minimizes variance over constant componentwise clean-comparison weights.

Theorem 3.2 derives the covariate-specific optimal efficient influence function and efficiency bound for staggered DiD, while Theorem 4.1 establishes consistency, asymptotic normality, and attainment for the resulting estimator.

Theorem 2 identifies the panel DDD target, Theorem 3 identifies the repeated-cross-section target, Theorem 5 derives the panel efficient influence function, and Theorem 7 derives the repeated-cross-section efficient influence function.
Theorem 5.2 gives variance-minimizing conditional GMM instruments when the conditional covariance is singular and a consistent linear system exists.
Theorem 6.3 derives a fixed-weight stacked-DDD limit law and accounts for dependence from comparison units shared across stacks.
The paper derives an efficient imputation estimator under its event-study model and notes applications to triple-difference designs.
Theorem 3.1 establishes asymptotic linearity and Gaussian approximation for cross-fitted estimators based on orthogonal scores.

body.tldr: The target is a fixed aggregate of staggered-DDD group--time effects under the literal global Ortiz--Villavicencio--Sant'Anna conditions.  At each post period \(u\), the published class uses every cohort \(c>u\), generating an OVS normal vector \(Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}\) that can strictly contain the old clean-through-terminal normal.  Exhausting that tangent normal gives \(\phi_{\mathrm{OVS},P}=\psi_P^0-r_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X)'K_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X)^\dagger Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}\) and \(V_{\mathrm{OVS}}\le V_{\mathrm{can}}\), where \(V_{\mathrm{can}}\) is now explicitly the larger localized-model bound.  Conditional loading \(b^\star(X)'\Psi_P\) remains only the aggregate score-family optimum unless it satisfies the full OVS projection equation.  A cross-fitted exhaustive-normal estimator attains \(V_{\mathrm{OVS}}\) with pointwise Wald inference for fixed finite-support covariates.  In that same regime the comparator gap is a finite-dimensional smooth fixed-rank functional and supports pointwise inference away from equality; continuous-covariate and equality-boundary gap inference remain open.  The bounded binary witness retains its exact \(3/512\) full-bound gain because its single local normal already spans the OVS normal.

project_justification.gap: Ortiz--Villavicencio and Sant'Anna impose DDD-CPT globally over every treated cohort, post period, and cohort clean at that period, but their estimator combines terminally clean pairwise scores with constant componentwise weights and does not derive the published observed tangent space or efficiency bound.  Existing staggered-DiD efficiency theory does not supply the coupled eligibility-gap full-data extension, denominator correction, or shared-cell DDD normal system.
project_justification.niche: The global published class contains period-admissible restrictions that disappear if controls are required to remain clean through a selected terminal target.  This creates three distinct precision frontiers: conditional pairwise-score loading, the larger localized equality model, and the smaller published OVS model.
project_justification.fill: The note proves full-data-to-observed equivalence for the literal OVS indexing, constructs deterministic local and OVS incidence bases, exhausts both tangent normals, and derives their singular Moore--Penrose projections.  It proves \(V_{\mathrm{OVS}}\le V_{\mathrm{can}}\le V_{\mathrm{agg}}\), supplies exact equality diagnostics, and attains the published bound with an orthogonal cross-fitted correction on fixed finite support.  It also supports fixed-law delta-method inference for positive comparator gaps in that regime and preserves the bounded \(3/512\) regression-test witness.

body.related_work: Ortiz--Villavicencio and Sant'Anna supply the causal assumptions, pairwise doubly robust scores, and constant componentwise GMM benchmark.  Their DDD-CPT assumption is global in period-admissible controls, whereas the earlier draft analyzed only a clean-through-terminal localization.  The present result exhausts the additional published normal rows and proves the corresponding smaller bound.  Chen, Sant'Anna, and Xie provide related conditional-efficiency geometry for staggered DiD, but not the DDD full-data extension, eligibility-gap incidence system, or shared target-share derivatives.  Newey motivates generalized-inverse conditional-moment geometry; here range inclusion, nested projections, rank recovery, and the fixed-support remainder are derived for the DDD objects.  Generic DML results motivate cross-fitting, while the orthogonal OVS signal and all shared-cell products are established directly.  The bounded binary construction remains a full-bound comparison because its unique nonzero clean-comparison row spans both the localized and OVS tangent normals.
body.technical_internal_limitation: Population canonicality is pointwise at a conditional-mean interior law.  Moore--Penrose projection permits singular and redundant normal coordinates because only the fitted normal random variable is identified.  Statistical attainment and positive efficiency-gap inference are proved only for fixed finite covariate support, fixed-law rank recovery, separated positive fixed-law spectra, fourth moments, and nondegenerate limiting variances; neither result is uniform over rank changes.  Gap inference is restricted to \(\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp}}\ge\delta_0>0\), because the first derivative can degenerate on the equality boundary.  A growing-sieve Riesz representation remains a population/general-covariate device and does not establish continuous-covariate Wald inference.
body.honest_scope: The causal class is the global OVS class, not the larger target-localized analogue.  The note separately reports the localized bound to quantify the information added by cohorts that are clean only at earlier periods.  The published canonical gradient and bound are population pointwise results.  Their cross-fitted attainment, variance consistency, and Wald coverage hold for fixed finite-support covariates with support masses bounded below, training-cell averages, and \(\tau_n=n^{-a}\), \(0<a<1/4\).  Positive comparator-gap inference uses the same finite-dimensional fixed-support regime, locally stable ranks, positive gap and influence variance, and thresholded Moore--Penrose systems.  Continuous-covariate attainment, continuous-covariate gap Wald inference, equality-boundary tests, and rank-uniform inference are not claimed.  The \(3/512\) witness remains a published full-bound result only because its one-normal closure equality is proved.
body.interpretation: A cohort can be a valid OVS control at an early period \(u\) even if it adopts before a target's terminal period \(t\).  Those early-period cells cannot enter a single cumulative terminally clean pairwise score, but they do create valid restriction normals and can lower the information bound.  Thus \(b^\star(X)'\Psi_P\) solves the aggregate conditional GLS problem, \(\phi_{\mathrm{can},P}\) solves the larger clean-through-terminal model, and \(\phi_{\mathrm{OVS},P}\) solves the literal published model.  A comparator is fully efficient only when its conditional cross-moment with \(Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}\) vanishes.  The optional \(\texttt{triplediff}\) backend should expose the exhaustive-normal method only for supported discrete-covariate designs, report aggregate and full diagnostics separately, and retain the user's prespecified \(\omega\).
